source.title: Unsupervised discovery of functional sequence patterns from protein language model with MotifAE
source.authors: Chao Hou; Di Liu; Yu-Feng Shen

page_placements.theme: Multi-response units often respond to related, co-occurring or look-alike concepts

record.file_problem: none; the full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study interprets individual MotifAE features against functional motifs and reports a feature matching multiple motif annotations that share a C-terminal location, refining the idea that multiple matches necessarily mean unrelated functions. It does not test polysemanticity in the original InceptionV1 neuron or transformer MLP neurons.
record.gate_note: The study reports that MotifAE features vary in granularity and that f27416 matches multiple C-terminal motifs. Other motif- and domain-identification results, including comparisons with standard SAE, do not measure whether a neuron responds to unrelated inputs and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders, with and without a smoothness loss, on ESM2-650M final-layer embeddings. It reports how well the SAE latent features match protein motifs, domains and DMS data. It never measures whether ESM2's own neurons respond to unrelated inputs, never frames its results as polysemanticity, and compares its method only against a standard SAE. The SAE framing relies on the 'linear combination of features' (superposition-style) premise without testing it. The multi-motif counts concern SAE dictionary latents, which are the study's own method output, not model neurons. So no version, including V6, is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that the smoothness loss improves motif and domain identification over a standard SAE. They also conclude that MotifAE features vary in granularity: some are function-specific, others capture more general shared functions such as C-terminal location (f27416). They do not discuss neuron polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse autoencoders on protein-language-model embeddings and evaluates features against protein motifs; it is not the original neuron-visualization method. MotifAE adds a sequence smoothness loss to standard SAE.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that adding a smoothness loss increases coherent feature activations and improves known-motif identification compared with standard SAE; it does not test how this changes polysemantic-neuron frequency.

fits_no_version.finding: Of 146 MotifAE SAE latents matching ELM motifs (AUROC > 0.9), 55 match multiple motifs. The most prominent, f27416, matches 17 motifs that all lie at the protein C-terminus. It has no predictive power for non-C-terminal motifs and fires at the C-terminus in 96% of proteins with C-terminal motifs versus 39% of random proteins.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents on protein LM embeddings that match several annotated motifs often capture one shared, coarser property (e.g. C-terminal position) rather than unrelated functions; i.e. feature granularity varies.

record.peer_reviewed: Nature Communications (Article in Press; peer review information is stated).
record.problems: The evidence concerns MotifAE latent features and curated protein motif annotations, not the responses of the underlying pLM neurons to unrelated inputs. The article does not establish that motifs sharing a C-terminal location have the same biological function.

untested.parts: Share of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer LMs, and variation across layers. ESM2 neurons are not examined.
Superposition as the cause. It is assumed by the SAE framing but not tested.
Polysemantic-neuron share under different architecture, activation function or regularization. The smoothness loss changes SAE features, not neuron polysemanticity.
Re-examination of canonical polysemantic neurons with better tools. Only SAE latents are interpreted.
Dependence of polysemanticity judgments on activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5 on V6' is overturned. V6 concerns canonical polysemantic neurons re-read with better tools. This paper analyses SAE dictionary latents, its own method, against motif annotations, and does not relate them to ESM2 neurons. All rows set to none and cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: Vision classifiers and image inputs, including InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55.
Transformer language-model MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and variation across transformer layers.
Whether superposition or capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.

The share of polysemantic neurons under different architectures, activation functions, or regularization, and whether that share can be lowered without substantial performance loss. The study compares MotifAE smoothness regularization with standard SAE but does not measure polysemantic-neuron share.

The study examines MotifAE latent features against protein motif annotations, not canonical neurons in vision models or transformer MLPs; it does not establish whether the underlying pLM neuron responses themselves share these functions.
Whether polysemanticity conclusions depend on activation range or explanation-scoring method.

relation.reason: It uses the SAE approach, whose stated core assumption is that embeddings are linear combinations of many features. It never tests neuron polysemanticity and never mentions it.

tranche.reason: It trains SAE latents (40,960) on ESM2-650M embeddings (1280 dims) as a tool and reports only its own method's motif and domain performance. It never measures whether ESM2 neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so the reader's T5 does not hold.

source_check.notes: f27416's 17 matched motifs all share the C-terminal position, so they are related, not unrelated. It is an SAE latent, not a neuron, so it is at most weak, indirect evidence on V6. The main figures use the window-size-3 MotifAE trained on raw ESM2-650M embeddings.

statements.correction: 146 MotifAE features match ELM motifs at AUROC > 0.9: 91 match one motif, 55 match several. f27416 is one of the most prominent multi-motif features and matches 17 motifs, all at the protein C-terminus. These are SAE latents, not ESM2 neurons.
statements.problem: Calls f27416 'the most prominent' multi-motif feature. The text says only that it is 'one of the most prominent', and Fig. 3E bins counts at >=5, so 17 is not shown to be the maximum.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MotifAE feature f27416 and the ELM motif evaluation
reader_labels.reason: f27416 matches multiple motifs that are all C-terminal, has no predictive power for non-C-terminal motifs, and is more often C-terminally activated in proteins with known C-terminal motifs than in random proteins (R1–R3). This supports a shared positional association rather than demonstrating unrelated mixtures.
